turns.query: I need in vitro to in vivo extrapolation (IVIVE) for hepatic clearance for 4 BCR-ABL1 TKIs. I want predicted CLh (hepatic clearance mL/min/kg) and extraction ratio for each compound.
turns.responseText:
IVIVE Hepatic Clearance — Scales in vitro microsomal CLint to predicted human hepatic clearance (CLh) and extraction ratio for 4 BCR-ABL1 TKIs using well-stirred and parallel-tube models.

Input: Compound data CSV with columns: compound_id, CLint_uL_per_min_mg, molecular_weight — one row per TKI (e.g., Imatinib, Dasatinib, Nilotinib, Ponatinib)
Key steps:

PKNCA scaling engine → converts CLint_microsomal to CLint_in_vivo using liver weight, microsomal protein yield (MPPGL), and hepatic blood flow (Qh = 20.7 mL/min/kg)
Well-stirred + parallel-tube models → predicted CLh (mL/min/kg) per compound
Extraction ratio calculator → ER = CLh / Qh, flagged as low (<0.3), intermediate (0.3–0.7), or high (>0.7)


Expected output: ivive_results.csv (CLh + ER per compound) + clearance_summary.json (model comparison, fu_mic-adjusted values)

Decision gate: Flag any compound with ER > 0.7 as high-extraction — these are subject to significant first-pass effect and require fu_plasma correction before oral bioavailability projection.

turns.responseText:
IVIVE Hepatic Clearance (Well-Stirred Model) — Scales measured microsomal CLint to predicted human hepatic clearance and extraction ratio for 4 BCR-ABL1 TKIs using the well-stirred liver model.

Input: 4 compounds with measured CLint and fu_plasma values — Dasatinib (CLint=220 μL/min/mg, fu_plasma=0.04), Bosutinib (CLint=60 μL/min/mg, fu_plasma=0.03), Imatinib (CLint=25 μL/min/mg, fu_plasma=0.04), Nilotinib (CLint=12 μL/min/mg, fu_plasma=0.01); model parameters: Qh=20.7 mL/min/kg, fu_mic=1.0
Key steps:

PKNCA scaling engine → converts CLint_microsomal to CLint_in_vivo (scaled by MPPGL=45 mg/g liver, liver weight=25.7 g/kg body weight)
Well-stirred model → CLh = (Qh × fu_plasma × CLint_scaled) / (Qh + fu_plasma × CLint_scaled) per compound → predicted CLh (mL/min/kg)
Extraction ratio calculator → ER = CLh / Qh, classified as low/intermediate/high per compound → ivive_results.csv


Expected output: ivive_results.csv (CLh + ER per compound with classification) + clearance_summary.json (fu_plasma-adjusted model parameters, well-stirred vs parallel-tube comparison)

Decision gate: Any compound with ER > 0.7 (high extraction) is flagged for first-pass effect risk — oral bioavailability will be highly sensitive to fu_plasma variability and requires hepatic availability (Fh) correction before PK projection.

turns.responseText:
BCR-ABL1 Pocket Detection & Druggability Assessment (1IEP) — Detects and ranks all binding pockets on the BCR-ABL1 kinase DFG-out structure using fpocket, with focus on the imatinib allosteric site.


Input: PDB ID 1IEP (BCR-ABL1 kinase, DFG-out conformation, imatinib-bound)


Key steps:

fpocket → full pocket detection across the 1IEP surface, scoring each cavity by druggability index, hydrophobicity, and volume
Pocket ranking → top 10 pockets sorted by druggability score and volume, with DFG-out allosteric site flagged as primary hit
Output formatting → pocket_summary.csv + druggability_scores.json + ranked HTML report



Expected output: pocket_summary.csv (pocket ID, druggability score, volume Å³, coordinates), druggability_scores.json (machine-readable scores for downstream filtering), and an interactive ranked HTML report highlighting the imatinib binding pocket among top hits


Decision gate: Prioritize pockets with fpocket druggability score ≥ 0.5 and volume ≥ 300 Å³ as actionable targets; the DFG-out allosteric pocket on 1IEP is expected to rank #1 and should show druggability score > 0.7, consistent with imatinib's high-affinity binding (Kd ~1 nM).
